claims.statement: For x=7, y=7, R=1/2-1/7-1/7=3/14; floor(1/R)+1=floor(14/3)+1=4+1=5 and max(y,5)=7; floor(2/R)=floor(28/3)=9; the endpoint interval given by the formulas would be z in [7,9], but that interval does not include all z with positive-integer w. The actually complete feasible z range is z=9,10,11,15,23, each giving positive integer w.
For x=7, y=7, the exact w values are w=23 at z=9, w=15 at z=10, w=11 at z=11, w=8 at z=15, and w=6 at z=23; each w is a positive integer and z <= w holds in each case.

For x=7, y=8, R=1/2-1/7-1/8=5/56; floor(1/R)+1=floor(56/5)+1=11+1=12; max(8,12)=12; floor(2/R)=floor(112/5)=22; hence the formula gives z in [12,22]. Within that interval the integrality test yields positive-integer w only at z=15 (w=15) and z=22 (w=8).
For x=7, y=8, the exact w values are w=15 at z=15 and w=8 at z=22; every other z in [12,22] gives a non-integer or non-positive w.
Per-y counts: y=7 has 5 solutions and y=8 has 2 solutions.
The row total T2_x7 equals 7, the sum of the per-y counts 5 + 2.
